text:
maria: FYI customer ACME (CS-4821) reports a sudden spike of 403/connection errors to our API from their Private VPC after a maintenance window yesterday. They said it started ~2024-04-06 10:20 UTC. They suspect allowlist drift.

kevin: I pulled the logs — from their supplied request IDs we see TLS handshake failures and some requests returning 403 with our WAF msg. Example from their curl: `curl -sv https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` -> `* TLS handshake timeout` then later `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`

raj: Did they use an EIP-based allowlist? If their NAT changed it's common for AWS-managed NAT failover to pick new egress IPs.

maria: They confirmed they have a customer-side allowlist of our egress IPs (they asked for static IPs). We provided a set during onboarding, but they said "we didn't change anything; it just stopped working".

jessica: Can they share a traceroute / tcpdump? Also asked them to `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` from a host in their VPC to show current egress IPs.

maria: They sent results: `203.0.113.42` from several hosts and one host `203.0.114.7`. Our last published allowed list had `203.0.113.10-203.0.113.39` only. Looks like the NAT replaced the EIP range.

raj: Confirmed on our side — we rotated a managed NAT gateway yesterday for that customer as part of infra autoscale; during failover AWS allocated new ephemeral egress IPs for a short period before reattaching the original EIP. If customer's firewall is strictly pinned it can drop.

kevin: Root cause summary: NAT failover -> ephemeral egress IPs -> customer allowlist didn't include ephemeral addresses -> their FO-firewall dropped traffic -> resulting in TLS/timeouts and 403 when some degraded requests hit fallback paths.

jessica: Short-term mitigation: we gave ACME the current observed egress IPs and asked them to add a small CIDR /32 entries for the temporaries, plus their original EIP. Also suggested they add our published IP set (we can provide) or use DNS-based allowlist with FQDN + SNI-aware firewall which is more robust.

maria: We also suggested two infra fixes on our side: 1) tag customer with `static-egress-required` to avoid NAT replacement during maintenance, and 2) offer them a Dedicated/VPC endpoint with an assigned EIP (paid). They were ok with the temporary add and asked for an SLA option.

raj: Action items:
- raj: add `static-egress-required` flag to ACME environment to prevent autoscale-triggered NAT replacement (iam change+infra rollout) — ETA 2h.
- kevin: assemble the full current egress IP list and post to the CS ticket + tell ACME to add.
- jessica: document recommended customer-side firewall rules (allow FQDN via SNI, relax strict EIP pins, or use PrivateLink).

infra-bot: infra change created #infra-task-1297 by raj (status: open).

kevin: Quick repro steps we used to validate locally: 1) spin an ec2 in same AZ with NAT gw attached, 2) `curl -v` to our API while toggling EIP detach/attach on the NAT gateway, 3) observe ephemeral source IP changes with `curl https://ifconfig.co`. If firewall pins EIP you'll see rejects.

maria: Customer accepted the temporary allowlist update. They're going to implement the change now and will confirm. Ticket updated.

jessica: Follow-up note for docs: add a KB called "Private VPC: Egress IP changes and allowlist drift" that covers NAT failover behavior, recommended patterns (static EIP pinning, PrivateLink, SNI-based firewall rules), and our support checklist.

maria: I'll keep this thread updated. If ACME reports rejections after adding the new IPs, we'll escalate to infra-oncall.

kevin: Added the egress IPs to the ticket and CC'd their infra lead. Also added a snippet for customers to run: `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` and `curl -s https://ifconfig.co` so they can quickly verify egress IPs.

maria: Closing loop — ACME confirmed inbound requests are passing after they updated allowlist. They still want a path to avoid drift; sales engaged on Dedicated EIP add-on. Marking as resolved in CS-4821. :white_check_mark:
